steps.title: Implement the minibatch forward, backward and optimizer-step loop

blocks.text: Each minibatch needs its own forward pass, fresh gradient and parameter update.

Iterate for features, targets in loader inside each declared epoch, compute predictions with model(features), then loss_fn(predictions, targets). For every minibatch, use optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward() and optimizer.step() in order; the update must use that minibatch's current gradient. Collect scalar evidence with loss.item(). Keep batch counts in the epoch summary, including an incomplete batch rather than silently treating it as full.

Test valid, boundary and failure fixtures with assert predicates. A false predicate raises AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution. For a plain-SGD fixture, retain parameter values before the step and assert parameter_after − parameter_before agrees with −learning_rate × current_gradient under tolerance.

blocks.code:
import torch

for epoch in range(declared_epochs):
    batch_records = []
    for features, targets in loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        predictions = model(features)
        loss = loss_fn(predictions, targets)
        loss.backward()
        before = [p.detach().clone() for p in model.parameters()]
        gradients = [p.grad.detach().clone() for p in model.parameters()]
        optimizer.step()
        # This fixture uses plain SGD only.
        for p, old, gradient in zip(model.parameters(), before, gradients):
            assert torch.allclose(p.detach() - old, -learning_rate * gradient,
                                  rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
        batch_records.append((loss.item(), features.shape[0]))

blocks.text: With five observations and retained batches of sizes 2, 2 and 1, compute model outputs and loss for each aligned feature/target pair. For every minibatch, zero gradients, backpropagate that batch's loss and apply the optimizer step. Collect scalar loss.item() values with batch counts, so an epoch summary does not pretend all batches contain two observations. In the deterministic plain-SGD fixture, retain the pre-step parameter and compare its observed change with −learning_rate × current_gradient under tolerance. Test the loop's supplied valid, boundary and failure cases.
The repeated sequence is what links each batch to its intended current gradient, rather than using an accumulated leftover from another batch.

steps.title: Apply correct neural-network training and evaluation modes

blocks.text: Validation needs both the right layer behavior and disabled gradient recording.

Use model.train() during parameter training and model.eval() during validation; the mode changes behavior of layers such as dropout and batch normalization. Wrap validation prediction in with torch.no_grad(): to disable graph recording and avoid building gradients for validation. Separate the two controls: eval changes relevant layer behavior; no_grad controls gradient recording.

left.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
layer = nn.Dropout(p=declared_dropout_probability)
layer.train()
with torch.no_grad():
    training_output = layer(x)
# no_grad does not switch dropout behavior.
assert torch.all((training_output == 0) |
                 (training_output == x / (1 - layer.p)))

right.code:
layer.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    evaluation_output = layer(x)
assert torch.equal(evaluation_output, x)
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    validation_predictions = model(validation_features)
# Forward only: no optimizer.step().
model.train()

blocks.takeaway: Layer mode and graph recording are separate.

steps.title: Apply correct neural-network training and evaluation modes

blocks.text: eval() changes layer behavior; no_grad() changes graph recording. Neither replaces the other, and validation must not update parameters.

segments.label: Training and validation use two independent controls
segments.summary: Use model.train() before parameter training and model.eval() before validation. These settings change the behavior of layers such as dropout and batch normalization; leaving training behavior active can introduce unwanted variability into validation scores. Separately, wrap validation computation in torch.no_grad() to prevent gradient graph recording. Evaluation mode controls layer behavior, not graph recording. Each training epoch begins by restoring training mode, computing the forward pass and loss, clearing gradients, running backward, and stepping the optimizer. The separate validation block switches to evaluation mode and computes validation loss inside no_grad without updating parameters. Recording both losses keeps the training and validation measurements distinct.

steps.title: Save and reload neural-network weights for prediction

blocks.text: Preserving weights means checking the restored state and fixed-input predictions.

Use torch.save(model.state_dict(), path) to save learned parameters. Reconstruct the same compatible architecture before loading them. Load the saved parameter mapping with torch.load(path, weights_only=True), and apply model.load_state_dict(mapping) to the compatible model. Before predicting with restored weights, switch the model to eval().

Compare reloaded-model predictions with the original evaluation-mode predictions on the same fixture under explicit numerical tolerances. Test valid, boundary and failure fixtures with assert predicates. A false predicate raises AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution. Open the checkpoint with a binary file handle (with open(path, "wb") for saving and "rb" for loading), and pass that handle to torch.save or torch.load.
Verify preservation in two ways: compare corresponding state_dict entries and compare predictions on fixed inputs.

left.code:
import torch
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    original_predictions = model(fixture_inputs)
with open(path, "wb") as handle:
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), handle)

right.code:
restored = compatible_architecture()
with open(path, "rb") as handle:
    mapping = torch.load(handle, weights_only=True)
restored.load_state_dict(mapping)
restored.eval()
for key, value in model.state_dict().items():
    assert torch.allclose(value, restored.state_dict()[key], rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
with torch.no_grad():
    restored_predictions = restored(fixture_inputs)
assert torch.allclose(original_predictions, restored_predictions,
                      rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

blocks.takeaway: Verify state entries and fixed-input predictions.
